spots.name: Wat Arun
spots.summary: Wat Arun Ratchawararam Ratchawaramahawihan or Wat Arun is a Buddhist temple (wat) in the Bangkok Yai district of Bangkok, Thailand. It is situated in Thonburi on the west bank of the Chao Phraya River. The temple derives its name from the Hindu god Aruṇa, often personified as the rays of the rising sun.

names.ja: ワット・アルンラーチャワラーラーム

spots.name: Wat Pho
spots.summary: Wat Pho, also spelled Wat Po, is a Buddhist temple complex in the Phra Nakhon District, Bangkok, Thailand. It is on Rattanakosin Island, directly south of the Grand Palace. Known also as the Temple of the Reclining Buddha, its official name is Wat Phra Chetuphon Wimon Mangkhalaram Rajwaramahawihan.

names.ja: ワット・プラチェートゥポンウィモンマンカラーラーム

spots.name: Grand Palace
spots.summary: The Grand Palace is a complex of buildings at the heart of Bangkok, Thailand. The palace has been the official residence of the Kings of Siam since 1782. The king, his court, and his royal government were based on the grounds of the palace until 1925.

names.ja: 王宮

spots.name: Wat Phra Kaew
spots.summary: Wat Phra Kaew, commonly known in English as the Temple of the Emerald Buddha and officially as Wat Phra Si Rattana Satsadaram, is regarded as the most sacred Buddhist temple in Thailand. The complex consists of a number of buildings within the precincts of the Grand Palace in the historical centre of Bangkok.

names.ja: ワット・シーラッタナーサーサダーラーム

spots.name: Emerald Buddha
spots.summary: The Emerald Buddha is an image of the meditating Gautama Buddha seated in a meditative posture, made of a semi-precious green stone, clothed in gold, and about 66 centimetres (26 in) tall. The image is considered the sacred palladium of Thailand.

names.ja: エメラルド仏

spots.name: Wat Suthat
spots.summary: Wat Suthat Thepphawararam is a Buddhist temple in Bangkok, Thailand. It is classified as a first-class royal temple, one of ten such temples in Bangkok. It is a temple located within the Inner Rattanakosin area, distinguished by the Giant Swing that stands directly in front of it.

names.ja: ワット・スタットテープワララーム

spots.name: Golden Buddha
spots.summary: The Golden Buddha, officially titled Phra Phuttha Maha Suwanna Patimakon, commonly known in Thai as Phra Sukhothai Traimit, is a gold Maravijaya Attitude seated Buddharupa statue, with a weight of 5.5 tonnes. It is located in the temple of Wat Traimit, Bangkok, Thailand.

spots.name: Wat Saket
spots.summary: Wat Saket Ratchawora Mahawihan, commonly known as Wat Saket, is a Buddhist temple (wat) in the Pom Prap Sattru Phai district of Bangkok, Thailand.

names.ja: ワット・サケート

spots.name: Wat Benchamabophit
spots.summary: Wat Benchamabophit Dusitvanaram is a Buddhist temple (wat) located in the Dusit District of Bangkok, Thailand. Also known as the Marble Temple, it is one of the city's most renowned religious landmarks and a major tourist attraction.

names.ja: ワット・ベンチャマボーピットドゥシットワナーラーム

photo.author: The original uploader was NamKhaeng at French Wikipedia.

spots.name: Wat Ratchabophit
spots.summary: Wat Rajabopit, or formally Wat Rajabopit Sathitmahasimaram Ratchaworawihan, is a Buddhist temple on Fueang Nakhon Road, Bangkok, along Khlong Khu Mueang Doem, not far from Wat Pho and the Grand Palace. The temple was built during the reign of King Chulalongkorn.

names.ja: ワット・ラーチャボーピットマハーシーマーラーム

spots.name: Wat Bowonniwet Vihara
spots.summary: Wat Bowaniwet Wihan Ratchaworawihan is a major Buddhist temple (wat) in Phra Nakhon district, Bangkok, Thailand. Being the residence of Nyanasamvara Suvaddhana, the late Supreme Patriarch of Thailand, it is the final resting place of two former kings of the Chakri Dynasty: King Vajiravudh and King Bhumibol Adulyadej.

names.ja: ワット・ボーウォンニウェート

photo.author: Fotograf / Photographer: Heinrich Damm (User:Hdamm, Hdamm at de.wikipedia.org)

spots.name: Wat Ratchanatdaram
spots.summary: Wat Ratchanatdaram is a Buddhist temple (wat) located at the intersection between Ratchadamnoen Klang and Maha Chai Road, in Phra Nakhon district, Bangkok. Meaning Temple of the Royal Niece, the temple was built to the order of King Nangklao for his granddaughter, Princess Somanass Waddhanawathy in 1846.

spots.name: Democracy Monument
spots.summary: The Democracy Monument is a public monument in the city centre of Bangkok, capital of Thailand. It occupies a traffic circle on the wide east–west Ratchadamnoen Avenue, at the intersection of Dinso Road.

names.ja: 民主記念塔

spots.name: Bangkok National Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Bangkok National Museum is the main branch museum of the National museums in Thailand and also one of the largest museums in Southeast Asia. It features exhibits of Thai art and history. It occupies the former palace of the vice king, set between Thammasat University and the National Theater, facing Sanam Luang.

names.ja: バンコク国立博物館

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Supanut Arunoprayote. Feel free to use any of my images,

spots.name: Giant Swing
spots.summary: The Giant Swing, also known as Sao Chingcha or Sao Ching Cha, is a 21.15 m (69.4 ft)-tall, swing-shaped religious structure and a prominent landmark in the Sao Chingcha Subdistrict of Phra Nakhon District, Bangkok, Thailand.

names.ja: サオチンチャー

spots.name: Victory Monument
spots.summary: Victory Monument is a military monument in Bangkok, Thailand. The monument was erected in June 1941 to commemorate the Thai victory in the Franco-Thai War.

names.ja: 戦勝記念塔

spots.name: CentralWorld
spots.summary: CentralWorld, is a shopping plaza and complex in the Siam area of Bangkok, in Thailand, opened in 1989. It is the ninth-largest shopping center in the world. The complex, which includes a hotel and office tower, is owned by Central Pattana.

names.ja: セントラルワールド

spots.name: Hua Lamphong railway station
spots.summary: Bangkok railway station is a railway station in Pathum Wan, the former central passenger terminal in Bangkok and the former railway hub of Thailand. It is in the center of the city in the Pathum Wan district, and is operated by the State Railway of Thailand (SRT).

names.ja: フワランポーン駅

spots.name: Soi Cowboy
spots.summary: Soi Cowboy is a short street (soi) in Bangkok, Thailand. It is 150 metres long and is the location of around 40 commercial establishments, mostly go-go bars. It caters mainly to tourists and expatriates.

names.ja: ソイ・カウボーイ

spots.name: Iconsiam
spots.summary: Iconsiam is a mixed-use development on the banks of the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok, Thailand. It includes a large shopping mall, which opened to the public on 9 November 2018, as well as hotels and residences.

names.ja: アイコンサイアム

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Supanut Arunoprayote. Feel free to use any of my images,

spots.name: Wat Mahathat Yuwaratrangsarit

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Mahathat Yuwaratrangsarit is a Buddhist temple in Bangkok, Thailand. It is one of only six first-class royal temples of the ratchaworamahawihan grade in Thailand. Its monks belong to the Mahā Nikāya.

names.ja: ワット・マハータートユワラートランサリット

spots.name: Wat Pathum Wanaram
spots.summary: Wat Pathum Wanaram or Wat Pathum for short is a Buddhist temple in Bangkok, Thailand. It is located in the Pathum Wan District, between the two shopping malls Siam Paragon and CentralWorld, and across the street of Siam Square.

names.ja: ワット・パトゥムワナーラーム

spots.name: Wat Ratchaorasaram

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Ratchaorasaram, often called shortened to Wat Ratchaorot (วัดราชโอรส) is an ancient Thai Buddhist temple in Bangkok.

names.ja: ワット・ラーチャオーロサーラーム

spots.name: Khaosan Road
spots.summary: Khaosan Road or Khao San Road is a 410 m (1,350 ft)-long street in central Bangkok, Thailand, constructed in 1892 during the reign of Rama V. It is in the Bang Lamphu area of Phra Nakhon District about 1 km (0.62 mi) north of the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew.

names.ja: カオサン通り

spots.name: Erawan Shrine
spots.summary: The Erawan Shrine, formally the Thao Maha Phrom Shrine, is a shrine in Bangkok, Thailand, which houses a statue of Phra Phrom, the Thai representation of Brahma, the Hindu god of creation. The name also refers to Mahabrahma, the ruler of the Brahma realm in Buddhist cosmology.

names.ja: エーラーワンの祠

spots.name: Lumphini Park
spots.summary: Lumphini Park, also Lumpini or Lumpinee, is a 360 rai park in Bangkok, Thailand. The park offers rare open public space, trees and playgrounds in the Thai capital and contains an artificial lake where visitors can rent boats.

names.ja: ルンピニー公園

spots.name: Wat Traimit

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Traimit Witthayaram Worawihan is a Theravada Buddhist temple (wat) in Samphanthawong district, the Chinatown area of the Thai capital Bangkok. Probably dating to the early Rattanakosin period, it was previously known as Wat Sam Chin (วัดสามจีน) and received its current name in 1940.

names.ja: ワット・トライミット

spots.name: Wat Bowon Sathan Sutthawat

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Bowon Sathan Sutthawat is a Buddhist temple in Bangkok, Thailand. It is a historic temple located within the grounds of the Front Palace, similar in function to Wat Phra Kaew inside the Grand Palace. Because the temple is situated within a royal palace, it has no resident monks.

spots.name: Sanam Luang
spots.summary: Sanam Luang, officially Thong Sanam Luang, is a 74.5 rai (119,200 m2) open field and public square in front of Wat Phra Kaew and the Grand Palace, Bangkok, Thailand. Sanam Luang is in the Phra Nakhon District, the historic center of Bangkok.

names.ja: サナーム・ルアン

spots.name: Wat Kanlayanamit

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Kalayanamitr Varamahavihara is a Buddhist temple (wat) in Bangkok, Thailand. The temple is located in Wat Kanlaya sub-district, on the Thonburi bank of the Chao Phraya River. The temple was established in 1825 by Chaophraya Nikonbodin, a wealthy Thai Chinese trader, who donated the temple to Rama III.

names.ja: ワット・カラヤナミトル

photo.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

spots.name: Jim Thompson House
spots.summary: The Jim Thompson House is a museum in central Bangkok, Thailand, housing the art collection of American businessman and architect James Harrison Wilson Thompson or simply Jim Thompson, the museum designer and former owner. Built in 1959, the museum spans one rectangular rai of land.

names.ja: ジム・トンプソンの家

spots.name: Patpong
spots.summary: Patpong is an entertainment district in Bangkok's Bang Rak District, Thailand, catering mainly, though not exclusively, to foreign tourists and expatriates. Patpong is internationally known as a red light district at the heart of Bangkok's sex industry.

names.ja: パッポン通り

spots.name: Wat Intharam

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Intharam Worawihan, also commonly known in short as Wat Intharam is a third-class royal temple in the area of Bang Yi Ruea, Thon Buri District, Bangkok. This temple is recognized as "the temple of King Taksin the Great" (1767–1782).

photo.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

spots.name: Wat Paknam Bhasicharoen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Paknam Bhasicharoen is a royal wat ('temple') located in Phasi Charoen district, Bangkok, at the Chao Phraya River. It is part of the Maha Nikaya fraternity and is the origin of the Dhammakaya tradition. It is a large and popular temple, supported by prosperous community members.

names.ja: パークナム

spots.name: Wat Rakhang
spots.summary: Wat Rakhangkhositaram is a second-class royal monastery in Bangkok, Thailand. It's located at 250/1 Arun Amarin Road, Siri Rat subdistrict, Bangkok Noi district, Thonburi side on the west bank of Chao Phraya River near Siriraj Hospital, Wang Lang Market and Ban Khamin Junction.

names.ja: ワット・ラカンコーシターラーム

photo.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

spots.name: Wat Ratchapradit

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Ratchapradit Sathit Mahasimaram Ratcha Wora Maha Viharn is a Buddhist temple in the Phra Nakhon District of Bangkok. Wat Ratchaparadit was designated a first-class royal monastery in 1915, making it one of the most significant temples in Thailand.

names.ja: ワット・プラディットサティットマハーシーマーラーム

photo.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

spots.name: Dusit Palace
spots.summary: Dusit Palace is a compound of royal residences in Bangkok, Thailand. The palace was constructed over a large area north of Rattanakosin Island between 1897 and 1901 by King Chulalongkorn.

names.ja: ドゥシット宮殿

spots.name: Wat Prayurawongsawat
spots.summary: Wat Prayurawongsawat Worawihan, known in short as Wat Prayun is a 19th century Buddhist temple complex, located near the Memorial Bridge in Bangkok, Thailand.

names.ja: ワット・プラユラウォンサーワート

spots.name: Sukhumvit Road
spots.summary: Sukhumvit Road, or Highway 3, is a major road in Thailand, and a major surface road of Bangkok and other cities. It follows a coastal route from Bangkok to Khlong Yai District, Trat border to Koh Kong, Cambodia.

names.ja: スクムウィット通り

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Waerth assumed (based on copyright claims).

spots.name: Memorial Bridge
spots.summary: The Memorial Bridge is a bascule bridge over the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok, Thailand, connecting the districts of Phra Nakhon and Thonburi.

names.ja: サパーン・プラプッタヨートファー

spots.name: Ananta Samakhom Throne Hall
spots.summary: The Ananta Samakhom Throne Hall is a royal reception hall in Dusit Palace in Bangkok, Thailand. It was commissioned by King Chulalongkorn in 1908. The building was completed in 1915, five years after Rama V's death in 1910. It is now employed from time to time for state occasions.

names.ja: アナンタサマーコム宮殿
names.zh: 阿南达沙玛空皇家御会馆

spots.name: Phra Phuttha Sihing

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Phra Phuttha Sihing is a highly revered image of the Gautama Buddha in Bangkok, Thailand, second in importance only after the Emerald Buddha. The image is currently housed at the Phutthaisawan Hall, now the Bangkok National Museum.

photo.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

spots.name: Wat Yannawa
spots.summary: Wat Yannawa, commonly known in English as "the boat temple", is a Buddhist temple (Wat) in Bangkok on Charoen Krung Road, Sathon district. The temple has a long history from the Ayutthaya era to the present.

spots.name: Wat Hong Rattanaram

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Hong Rattanaram Ratchaworawihan, or just called Wat Hong Rattanaram is an ancient Thai Buddhist temple located in Bangkok rim the Khlong Bangkok Yai canal. It is classified as the second rank of royal temple and can be considered a temple of Prince Pinklao.

names.ja: ワット・ホンラタナーラーム

photo.author: กสิณธร ราชโอรส

spots.name: Yaowarat Road
spots.summary: Yaowarat Road in Samphanthawong District is the main artery of Bangkok's Chinatown. Modern Chinatown now covers a large area around Yaowarat and Charoen Krung Road.

names.ja: ヤワラー通り

spots.name: Wat Intharawihan
spots.summary: Wat Intharawihan or Wat Intharavihan is a Third Class Royal wat (temple) located in the Phra Nakhon District of Bangkok, Thailand.

spots.name: Assumption Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Assumption Cathedral is the principal Catholic church of Thailand, located at 23 Oriental Avenue, New Road, in the Bang Rak District of Bangkok. It is the main church of the Archdiocese of Bangkok. The cathedral hosted both of the papal visits to Thailand: Pope John Paul II in 1984 and Pope Francis in 2019.

names.ja: アサンプション大聖堂

spots.name: Devasathan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Devasathan or Royal Brahmin Office of Thai Royal Court is a Hindu temple near Wat Suthat in the Phra Nakhon District, Bangkok, Thailand. The temple is the official centre of Hinduism in Thailand.

spots.name: Phaya Thai Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Phya Thai Palace or Royal Phya Thai Palace is on the banks of the Samsen Canal on Rajavithee Road in the Ratchathewi District of Bangkok.

spots.name: Wat Thepthidaram

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Thepthidaram Worawihan or popularly known as Wat Thepthidaram is a third grade royal Buddhist temple in Worawihan type, located in the area known as Pratu Phi or official name Samran Rat, Bangkok, near Mahakan Fort and Wat Ratchanadda.

spots.name: Wat Rachathiwat

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Rachathiwat Ratchaworawihan (วัดราชาธิวาสราชวรวิหาร) or simply Wat Rachathiwat, is a second-class royal monastery of the ratchaworawihan type, located on the east bank of the Chao Phraya River in the Wachiraphayaban subdistrict of Dusit, Bangkok.

names.ja: ワット・ラーチャーティワートウィハーン

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Supanut Arunoprayote. Feel free to use any of my images,

spots.name: Wat Chana Songkhram
spots.summary: Wat Chanasongkhram, commonly shortened to Wat Chana Songkhram, is a second-class royal monastery of ratchaworamahawihan status. It is located in Chana Songkram Sub-district, Phra Nakhon District, Bangkok, within the area of Bang Lamphu opposite Khaosan Road and adjacent to Rambuttri Road.

names.ja: ワット・チャナソンクラーム

spots.name: Royal Cemetery at Wat Ratchabophit
spots.summary: The Royal Cemetery is located at the western side of the grounds of Wat Ratchabophit in Bangkok.

spots.name: Sathorn Unique Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sathorn Unique Tower is an unfinished skyscraper located in the Sathon district of Bangkok, Thailand. Planned as a high-rise condominium complex, construction of the building was halted during the 1997 Asian financial crisis, when it was already about 80 percent complete.

names.ja: サトーンユニークタワー

spots.name: Vimanmek Mansion

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Vimanmek Mansion is a former royal villa in Bangkok, Thailand. It is in the Dusit Palace complex in Dusit District. As of 2019 it has been dismantled to allow for foundation repairs and will be rebuilt upon its completion.

names.ja: ウィマーンメーク宮殿

spots.name: Sri Maha Mariamman Temple, Bangkok
spots.summary: Sri Maha Mariamman Temple, also known as Maha Uma Devi Temple (Thai: วัดพระศรีมหาอุมาเทวี; RTGS: Wat Phra Si Maha Umathewi and Wat Khaek in Thai, is a South Indian architecture style Hindu temple on Si Lom Road in Bangkok, Thailand. It was built in 1879 by Vaithi Padayatchi, a Tamil Hindu immigrant.

spots.name: Bang Khun Phrom Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bang Khun Phrom Palace is a former royal residence in Bangkok, Thailand. It served as the residence of Prince Paribatra Sukhumbandhu until his forced exile following the Siamese revolution of 1932.

spots.name: Thonburi Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Thonburi Palace, also known in Thai as Phra Racha Wang Derm, is the former royal palace of King Taksin, who ruled the Siamese (Thai) kingdom of Thonburi following the fall of Ayutthaya in 1767 and up until the establishment of Rattanakosin in 1782.

names.ja: 旧王宮

spots.name: Equestrian statue of King Chulalongkorn
spots.summary: Equestrian statue of Chulalongkorn the Great, otherwise known as Equestrian statue is an outdoor sculpture in cast bronze at the center of the Royal Plaza in Bangkok, Thailand, honoring King Chulalongkorn.

spots.name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre is a contemporary arts centre in Siam area, Bangkok, Thailand. Art, music, theatre, film, design and cultural/educational events take place in its exhibition and performance spaces. The centre includes cafes, commercial art galleries, bookshops, craft shops, and an art library.

names.fr: Centre Culturel et Artistique de Bangkok
names.ja: バンコク芸術文化センター

spots.name: Phra Sumen Fort
spots.summary: Best viewed from Santichaiprakan Park, Phra Sumen Fort is one of two remaining towers of the historic city wall that once surrounded Rattanakosin Island completely (the other being Mahakan Fort). The historic city wall that followed the Chao Phraya River and Khlong Rop Krung used to have fourteen of these watchtowers, but twelve of them have not endured the test of time. Phra Sumen Fort was constr

spots.name: King's Birthday Celebration Arch
spots.summary: This Chinese-style ceremonial gate was built by Thais of Chinese descent to show their loyalty to King Bhumibol Adulyadej. It was officially inaugurated on his 72nd birthday on 5 December 1999. The four Chinese characters on the arch mean "Long Live The King" and are in the handwriting of HRH Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn (who is fluent in Chinese).

spots.name: Madame Tussaud's
spots.summary: A branch of the popular museum displaying waxworks of famous people. It features life-sized statues of HRH Prince Mahitala Thibed Adulyadej Vikrom Phra Baroma Rajajanok (The Prince Father), HRH Princess Srinagarindra (The Princess Mother) and other famous Thais. But there are also plenty of Western figures, including US president Barack Obama in the Oval Office and the English football player Stev

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Supanut Arunoprayote. Feel free to use any of my images,

spots.name: Thien Fa Foundation
spots.summary: This is the oldest charitable society of Bangkok, founded in 1902 by Chinese immigrants. The local clinics at the site provide free medical treatment for the poor using traditional Chinese as well as modern practices. Most interesting for foreign visitors is the courtyard which boasts the Guan Yin Shrine (ปูชนียสถานเจ้าแม่กวนอิม), commonly known as the "Shrine for the Goddess of Mercy". Local visi

spots.name: King Rama I the Great Monument
spots.summary: Built in commemoration of Bangkok's 150th anniversary celebrations in 1932, the monument is at the foot of the Great Memorial Bridge on the Bangkok side. King Rama I was the first king in the Royal House of Chakri and founder of Bangkok as the capital of the Kingdom of Siam, as Thailand was then known. He was born in Ayutthaya, one of Thailand's former capitals, on 20 March 1736. He ascended to th

spots.name: Santichaiprakan Park
spots.summary: This small, green park has a great view of the Chao Phraya River and the modern Rama VIII suspension bridge that crosses it. There's an open-air pavilion, the Phra Sumen Fort and (supposedly) the last two lamphu trees of the area (these trees used to be all over Banglamphu, as that's where the district got its name from). Activities held in the park include Thai classical music, juggling and (at 1

spots.name: Bangkok Bank Building
spots.summary: Opposite the Tang To Kang gold shop, and quite similar to it, the Bangkok Bank Building is one of Bangkok's oldest commercial buildings. The exterior is an example of classic early Rattanakosin-style with clear European influences. The interior is heavy with hardwood panelling.

spots.name: Tang To Kang Gold Shop

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Chinatown is one of Bangkok's oldest districts and about 14% of the buildings have been designated as historical landmarks. Tang To Kang is one of them, an interesting colonial-style building and actually the oldest gold shop of Bangkok (which is difficult to believe now with so many gold shops scattered over the district). If you want to see the gold museum, you have to make an appointment two da

spots.name: Wat Maha Phruettharam
spots.summary: You are far off the beaten path when visiting this old monastery, but it's definitely a sight for those interested in Buddhism. The exact origin of this temple is unknown, but it is believed to have originated from the early Rattanakosin era or late Ayutthaya period. It had several names, but got its permanent name during the reign of King Rama IV, who extensively renovated it and raised its statu

spots.name: Amorosa Bar and The Deck
spots.summary: Tourist flock to the rooftop bar Amorosa for its spectacular sunset views of Wat Arun. Get there early, as there are only 20 seats in the house and you can forget a seat after 18:00. The view comes at a price, expect to pay Western rates for alcoholic drinks. Downstairs is The Deck, a restaurant serving Thai and European food, also with a view of the temple. It is recommended to make a reservation

spots.name: Aquatini Bar & Restaurant
spots.summary: Part of the Navalai River Resort, this luxury restaurant with Thai and Western dishes has river views over the Chao Phraya River. The interior of the indoor bar has random postmodern touches. It's best to stick to outdoors though, as the deck gives the best views. The breeze, trees and light music make the ambience chilled out. Mostly foreigners visit this place, and the staff make it feel a bit l

spots.name: Chabad House Kosher Restaurant

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: This restaurant is part of an international Hasidic chain with more than 2,000 branches all over the world. It is ideal for Jewish travellers that keep kosher. There is a large meat menu with the opportunity to taste some great kosher Thai cuisine. Or get a schnitzel with hummus. Finally something different than the usual pad thai that's on every street corner! They also have a synagogue (services

spots.name: Chong Kee
spots.summary: Many of the eateries here specialise in one dish, and here pork satay with sweet toast is the only dish served. Forget the passable satay usually served from street carts, Chong Kee knows how to make this. The skewers here are smoky and tender, and fat cuts of pork are used. Lots of herbs and the right amount of chilis are used in the peanut sauce making it sweet as it's supposed to be. Try to avo

spots.name: DJ Station
spots.summary: The most famous gay nightclub in Bangkok and busy almost every night, with ladyboy show, disco, dance performance. Jam-packed on weekends, do not enter if you're even slightly claustrophobic. Most drinks are around 100-200 baht (be careful with spirits, the bartenders don't measure anything and tend to over-pour, sometimes badly), or buy a bottle of spirits from 1,000 baht up and get free mixers.

spots.name: Double Dogs Tea Room

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Tea lovers rejoice. This hidden gem has the best tea selection of Bangkok. Just picking a tea from the menu shows the wide array of varieties available. First the teas are split by country of origin and then roughly by colour. Picking a Chinese tea seems like an obvious choice, but there are also Japanese, Sri Lankan and Taiwanese varieties available. Ask the staff for a recommendation. It has a w

spots.name: Eiah Sae
spots.summary: As always in Yaowarat, this coffee joint does not sell the usual latte or cappuccino. The special treat is Chaozhou coffee, a bittersweet Chinese brew. It's locally famous for its coffee beans, which are roasted and blended following a secret family recipe. This place is over 80 years old and has been in the family for four generations. This place has a real character and still serves as a meeting

spots.name: Gaggan
spots.summary: Opened in 2010 by Gaggan Anand, an Indian chef who wanted to refine Indian dining to the level of French cuisine. And he has succeeded. Gaggan was ranked as the best restaurant in Asia in 2015, 2016 and 2017 by Restaurant magazine. In 2017, it was even ranked as 7th in the entire world. Anand and his restaurant were featured in season 2 of the Netflix documentary series Chef's Table. A session in

spots.name: Go-Ang Pratunam Chicken Rice
spots.summary: Formerly Kai Ton Pratunam, it initially seems like a simple street food vendor—but it is always crowded as the guests rave about the food. It is touted as having Bangkok's best chicken rice (ข้าวมันไก่ khao man kai), which is quite similar to Hainanese chicken rice. spots.name: Hua Seng Hong
spots.summary: The typical messy place you would expect around Yaowarat with fresh crabs and king prawns hanging out front. Inside it is a plain long hall and it is usually packed. Order the Chinese dishes, particularly the crab is worth it. spots.name: Krua Khun Kung
spots.summary: Tucked in a small alley, this restaurant is the only good restaurant close to the Grand Palace. Its odd location makes it often unnoticed by foreigner travellers, which is a shame as it has a great view over the Chao Phraya River. spots.name: L'Opera
spots.summary: Established 1984, this is the oldest genuine Italian restaurant in Bangkok, and most likely also in Thailand. Though long established as the Italian place to eat amongst the Thai stars, politicians and local business elite, the atmosphere is relaxed and caters to tourists and middle class as well. spots.name: Mu Kratha Heng Heng Korat
spots.summary: Excellent Thai barbecue hot pot. Extremely popular among locals, so you can expect a long wait (up to an hour), particularly on weekends, if you just show up. Your best bet is to make a reservation, which, assuming your Thai is subpar for a phone call, would involve walking up to the restaurant and making one in person. spots.name: Mulligans
spots.summary: Opened in 2009, this Irish pub has a daily promotion between 20:00 and 02:00, when a large beer or a cocktail sets you back 110 baht. The area downstairs is relaxed, and right beside the road, so a great place for talking and people-spotting. spots.name: Nai Sow
spots.summary: A Thai-Chinese restaurant that has been consistently excellent for the last 40 years. It used to be run by Mr. Sow at Sampheng Lane, but moved to its current location at Phlap Phla Chai intersection as his son took over business. Foreigners praise the tom yam kung, but the locals come here for pan-fried hoi tod (fried mussels with eggs). You can also try the muu sa-ded, pork rubbed with garlic. Th

spots.name: Nai Uan Yen Ta Fo

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: This simple restaurant is specialised in yen ta fo, a Chinese seafood dish that is also known as rice noodles in red tofu soup. It includes delicacies such as coagulated blood, pickled squid and fishballs. It has a distinctive pink colour because of the fermented soybean paste that is added to the meal. This place is locally well known, so prices are a little higher than similar noodle restaurants

spots.name: Prachak Restaurant
spots.summary: A very small restaurant that nevertheless managed to become famous by word of mouth. The owner is the fourth generation running this restaurant that is more than one hundred years old! No fancy banners, or even an English sign, just good food that is well known among the locals. Ordering is no problem as the menus have pictures shown. spots.name: Sawasdee House
spots.summary: Another people-watching spot, this time along Soi Rambuttri. The tables outside are good for conversation and people-watching, and you can smoke sheesha if you wish. You can also sit inside, but talking is more difficult as the music is very loud. The interior looks nice, with traditional Thai decoration all around. spots.name: Saxophone Pub
spots.summary: One of the best pubs to catch live playing jazz and blues bands. The interior is beautifully decorated with old guitars and cymbals. Even while it's crowded, the atmosphere is cosy. It is very much focused on experiencing the music, as the public sits and stands in a semicircle around the band. Don't come here for the food, as it is not great and overpriced. spots.name: Sky Bar Bangkok
spots.summary: The world's tallest rooftop bar/restaurant, a few metres higher up than Vertigo — but due to its slightly off-centre location, the views are arguably not quite as stunning. It's a complex of a number of expensive restaurants, including the Mediterranean-flavoured Sirocco, but the cheapest option for just a drink is the outdoor Sky Bar, which has a jazz band most nights.
